title: The null and undefined Types knowledge check

questions.prompt: With strictNullChecks enabled, how should a possibly missing value be handled?
options: Check or narrow it before using members that require a non-null value.
Assume it is present because the variable has a declared type.
Use non-null assertions on every access without checking.
Turn off strict checking for the entire project.
questions.answer_key: Check or narrow it before using members that require a non-null value.
questions.explanation: Strict null checking makes absence part of the type contract and encourages explicit handling.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “The null and undefined Types”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with optional values and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with optional values and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Optional values”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “The null and undefined Types”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check strict null checking, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume safely handling missing values is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check strict null checking, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Strict null checking”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
